questions.q: With the starting settings, when does the parachute open, how high up, and at what Mach number?
questions.do: Load the page and leave the three sliders where they are (entry angle 15.5°, steering 45°, parachute at Mach 2.04). Read the stat tiles under The descent, second by second.
questions.a: About 3.9 min after entry, 15.1 km up, at Mach 2.04. The verdict says “Ready for the sky crane”, because the parachute opened below its Mach 2.2 limit and high enough to slow down.

questions.q: What happens if the rover comes in too shallow, or too steep?
questions.do: Drag Entry angle at 125 km, below level all the way down to 10.0° and read the verdict. Then drag it up to 22.0° and read the Peak braking and Parachute opens tiles.
questions.a: At 10.0° it skips out: it bounces off the thin upper air and leaves Mars. At 22.0° it still reaches the sky crane, but peak braking jumps to about 17.7 g (from 10.0 g), and the parachute opens at about 2.0 min. Steeper means it hits thick air faster, so it brakes harder.

questions.q: What goes wrong if you open the parachute too early, while the rover is still very fast?
questions.do: Move Open the parachute at up to Mach 2.50 and read the verdict box.
questions.a: Parachute shredded. It opens at Mach 2.50, but it is rated for Mach 2.2 at most. Faster air would rip it apart.

questions.q: Why does the steering setting decide whether the rover survives?
questions.do: Set Steering: how far the lift is rolled away from straight up to 0° and read the tiles. Then set it to 180° and read the verdict.
questions.a: At 0° (lift up) the parachute opens about 5.8 min in, at about 13.1 km. At 180° (lift down) the verdict is “Crashed under the heat shield”. Lift pointed down makes it dive, so it reaches the ground before the thin air has slowed it enough to open the parachute.

questions.q: The page checks its model against the real Curiosity and Perseverance landings. How close does it get for peak heating and for leaving the backshell?
questions.do: Scroll to the table Checks against the real landings and read the rows Peak heating after entry and Leaving the backshell.
questions.a: Curiosity’s real peak heating came at 1 min 15 s; the model gives 66 s. Perseverance left the backshell at under 320 km/h at 1.9 km; the model gives 312 km/h at 1.9 km. So the simple model lands close to the real missions.
